title: Customer-scoped GeoRoute Orchestrator: allowlists, denylist gates and tiered model fallback
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Implement a customer-scoped GeoRoute Orchestrator that enforces EU-only routing and data-residency constraints while supporting per-customer allowlists/denylists and deterministic tier/model fallbacks. This ticket covers the rules engine, enforcement integration points (control-plane PDP + data-plane enforcer), audit/logging requirements, and a minimal config UI surface for PM/CS to update customer gates.

Problem statement: Several enterprise customers require strict EU data residency and region-only routing. Additionally, some customers want explicit allowlists (trusted regions/accounts) or deny policies (block certain regions or dedicated tiers). We must guarantee that requests from such customers never leave allowed geographies, and when a preferred model/tier is unavailable we must provide a policy-controlled fallback chain (e.g., same-region quantized variant -> same-region smaller model -> EU-compatible cross-region hot-standby with customer consent). Any policy decision must be auditable and reversible.

Proposed approach:
- Policy model: implement declarative per-customer RoutingPolicy objects in control plane with fields: residency_scope (e.g., eu-only), allowed_regions (list), denied_regions (list), allowed_tiers, fallback_chain (ordered list of model-tags), require_consent_for_cross_region_fallback (bool), audit_level (minimal|detailed). We'll persist policy as part of customer profile (encrypted at rest).
- Enforcement points:
  1) Pre-routing PDP in control plane: evaluate request metadata (customer_id, requested_region, requested_tier, model_id, metadata flags such as pii=true). Deny or short-circuit to error if policy blocks. Emit decision with decision_id.
  2) Data-plane enforcer in edge proxy/runtime: lightweight policy cache (decision_id -> allowed route) fetched from control plane with TTL. This prevents control-plane outage from stopping enforcement; the runtime will default to last-known policy and fail closed if policy indicates block.
  3) Fallback orchestration: when target node pool has no capacity, orchestrator consults fallback_chain to pick the next candidate model variant that satisfies residency and tier constraints.
- Observability & Auditing: every routing decision stores an immutable log entry with decision_id, policy_key, evaluated conditions, chosen_route, and whether fallback was used. These logs are forwarded to the existing Console audit pipeline with retention configurable per-customer.
- Config UI/Operator flow: small Console form to toggle eu-only, add/remove allowed/denied regions, reorder fallback chain, and toggle cross-region fallback consent. Changes emit a versioned policy and a rollout window (immediate or scheduled).

Trade-offs & risks considered:
- Strong enforcement at the edge increases latency slightly (RTT for policy cache refresh). Mitigation: TTL caching and pre-warming policies for high-traffic customers. We target <1ms added p95 for cached decisions.
- Stale policy vs fast propagation: we accept eventual propagation for non-critical changes; but for denylist adds we require immediate invalidation push. Implementation: support push invalidation for denylist/critical flags.
- Complexity of fallback chains: long chains can create unpredictable cost/quality outcomes. We will limit chain length to 3 by default and surface expected cost/delta to PM before applying.
- Security: storing per-customer policies requires KMS-wrapped storage and RBAC to restrict who in Console can edit. Security review required (ticket flag set).

Acceptance criteria:
- Control-plane API to create/read/update customer RoutingPolicy (CRUD) with validation tests.
- Runtime enforcer that consults a cached decision and rejects requests violating policy with 403 + structured error code geo_policy_violation.
- Fallback orchestrator that respects residency constraints and ordered fallback_chain; unit and integration tests demonstrating prioritized selection.
- Audit log entries emitted for each decision and visible in Console audit view for a test customer.
- Migration script to backfill existing enterprise customers with eu-only requirement into new policy object (dry-run mode first).

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag gated in control plane (flag: geo_orchestrator_v1). Deploy control-plane API and policy storage behind the flag.
2) Canary runtime rollout to 10% of Dedicated clusters with policy cache enabled. Monitor rejects and latency (dashboard: geo-routing-p95, geo-routing-fallback-rate).
3) Enable push invalidation and test denylist immediate behavior with internal test customers.
4) Gradual enablement for EU-sensitive customers via Customer Success-assisted migrations.

Longer-term: integrate with org-level data classification so policies can auto-apply when customer marks workloads as EU-resident or regulated. Also add fine-grained attribute matching (dataset tags) to choose model variants based on data sensitivity.
